passages.text: This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced upon the Israelites before his death.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a man of God.
Moses spoke a blessing.
Moses gave this blessing to the Israelites.
Moses blessed them before he died.
passages.original: וְזֹ֣את הַבְּרָכָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בֵּרַ֥ךְ מֹשֶׁ֛ה אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לִפְנֵ֖י מוֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He said: “The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon us from Seir; He shone forth from Mount Paran and came with myriads of holy ones, with flaming fire at His right hand.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the man of God.
Moses spoke to the Israelites before he died.
Moses said these words as a blessing.
The LORD is God.
The LORD came from Sinai.
The LORD appeared to the people at Sinai.
The LORD shone like the dawn from Seir.
The LORD shone forth from Mount Paran.
The LORD came with many holy ones.
The LORD had flaming fire at His right hand.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה מִסִּינַ֥י בָּא֙ וְזָרַ֤ח מִשֵּׂעִיר֙ לָ֔מוֹ הוֹפִ֙יעַ֙ מֵהַ֣ר פָּארָ֔ן וְאָתָ֖ה מֵרִבְבֹ֣ת קֹ֑דֶשׁ מִֽימִינ֕וֹ אֵשְׁדָּת לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: Surely You love the people; all the holy ones are in Your hand, and they sit down at Your feet; each receives Your words— the law that Moses gave us, the possession of the assembly of Jacob.
passages.sermon:
God loves His people.
God holds all His holy ones in His hand.
The holy ones sit at God's feet.
Each holy one receives God's words.
Moses gave us the law.
The law belongs to the assembly of Jacob.
passages.original: אַ֚ף חֹבֵ֣ב עַמִּ֔ים כָּל־ קְדֹשָׁ֖יו בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְהֵם֙ תֻּכּ֣וּ לְרַגְלֶ֔ךָ יִשָּׂ֖א מִדַּבְּרֹתֶֽיךָ׃ תּוֹרָ֥ה צִוָּה־ לָ֖נוּ מֹשֶׁ֑ה מוֹרָשָׁ֖ה קְהִלַּ֥ת יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: So the LORD became King in Jeshurun when the leaders of the people gathered, when the tribes of Israel came together.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is King in Jeshurun.
Jeshurun means Israel.
The leaders of the people gathered together.
All the tribes of Israel came together.
The LORD became their King at that time.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י בִישֻׁר֖וּן מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּהִתְאַסֵּף֙ רָ֣אשֵׁי עָ֔ם יַ֖חַד שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Let Reuben live and not die, nor his men be few.”
passages.sermon:
Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob.
Reuben was the ancestor of the tribe of Reuben.
Moses spoke a blessing over Reuben.
Moses said, "Let Reuben live."
Moses said, "Let Reuben not die."
Moses said, "Let Reuben's men be many."
passages.original: יְחִ֥י רְאוּבֵ֖ן וְאַל־ יָמֹ֑ת וִיהִ֥י מְתָ֖יו מִסְפָּֽר׃ס

passages.text: And concerning Judah he said: “O LORD, hear the cry of Judah and bring him to his people. With his own hands he defends his cause, but may You be a help against his foes.”
passages.sermon:
Judah is one of the tribes of Israel.
Moses spoke a blessing about Judah.
He said, “LORD, hear Judah’s voice.
Bring Judah to his people.
Judah uses his own hands to defend himself.
LORD, help Judah against his enemies.”
passages.original: וְזֹ֣את לִֽיהוּדָה֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ שְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ ק֣וֹל יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־ עַמּ֖וֹ תְּבִיאֶ֑נּוּ יָדָיו֙ רָ֣ב ל֔וֹ וְעֵ֥זֶר מִצָּרָ֖יו תִּהְיֶֽה׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Levi he said: “Give Your Thummim to Levi and Your Urim to Your godly one, whom You tested at Massah and contested at the waters of Meribah.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke about the tribe of Levi.
He said, “Lord, give Your Thummim to Levi.
Give Your Urim to Your faithful one.
You tested Levi at Massah.
You argued with him at the waters of Meribah.”
passages.original: וּלְלֵוִ֣י אָמַ֔ר תֻּמֶּ֥יךָ וְאוּרֶ֖יךָ לְאִ֣ישׁ חֲסִידֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִסִּיתוֹ֙ בְּמַסָּ֔ה תְּרִיבֵ֖הוּ עַל־ מֵ֥י מְרִיבָֽה׃

passages.text: He said of his father and mother, ‘I do not consider them.’ He disregarded his brothers and did not know his own sons, for he kept Your word and maintained Your covenant.
passages.sermon:
Levi is the subject of this passage.
Levi is faithful to God.
Levi says about his father and mother, “I do not consider them.”
Levi does not recognize his brothers.
Levi does not know his own sons.
Levi acts this way because he keeps God’s word.
Levi guards God’s covenant.
passages.original: הָאֹמֵ֞ר לְאָבִ֤יו וּלְאִמּוֹ֙ לֹ֣א רְאִיתִ֔יו וְאֶת־ אֶחָיו֙ לֹ֣א הִכִּ֔יר וְאֶת־ בָּנוֹ לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע כִּ֤י שָֽׁמְרוּ֙ אִמְרָתֶ֔ךָ וּבְרִֽיתְךָ֖ יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃

passages.text: He will teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel; he will set incense before You and whole burnt offerings on Your altar.
passages.sermon:
Levi is the subject of this blessing.
Levi will teach God's ordinances to Jacob.
Levi will teach God's law to Israel.
Levi will place incense before God.
Levi will offer whole burnt offerings on God's altar.
passages.original: יוֹר֤וּ מִשְׁפָּטֶ֙יךָ֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וְתוֹרָתְךָ֖ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יָשִׂ֤ימוּ קְטוֹרָה֙ בְּאַפֶּ֔ךָ וְכָלִ֖יל עַֽל־ מִזְבְּחֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Bless his substance, O LORD, and accept the work of his hands. Smash the loins of those who rise against him, and of his foes so they can rise no more.”
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Levi served God faithfully.
Levi kept God's word and covenant.
Moses prayed for Levi.
He said, "LORD, bless Levi's strength."
Accept the work Levi does with his hands.
Defeat those who attack Levi.
Strike down Levi's enemies so they cannot rise again.
passages.original: בָּרֵ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ חֵיל֔וֹ וּפֹ֥עַל יָדָ֖יו תִּרְצֶ֑ה מְחַ֨ץ מָתְנַ֧יִם קָמָ֛יו וּמְשַׂנְאָ֖יו מִן־ יְקוּמֽוּן׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Benjamin he said: “May the beloved of the LORD rest secure in Him; God shields him all day long, and upon His shoulders he rests.”
passages.sermon:
Benjamin is the subject of this blessing.
Benjamin is called the beloved of the LORD.
The LORD gives Benjamin safety.
Benjamin rests secure in the LORD.
God protects Benjamin all day long.
God shields Benjamin every moment.
Benjamin rests on God's shoulders.
God carries Benjamin close to Himself.
passages.original: לְבִנְיָמִ֣ן אָמַ֔ר יְדִ֣יד יְהֹוָ֔ה יִשְׁכֹּ֥ן לָבֶ֖טַח עָלָ֑יו חֹפֵ֤ף עָלָיו֙ כָּל־ הַיּ֔וֹם וּבֵ֥ין כְּתֵיפָ֖יו שָׁכֵֽן׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Joseph he said: “May his land be blessed by the LORD with the precious dew from heaven above and the deep waters that lie beneath, with the bountiful harvest from the sun and the abundant yield of the seasons, with the best of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills, with the choice gifts of the land and everything in it, and with the favor of Him who dwelt in the burning bush. May these rest on the head of Joseph and crown the brow of the prince of his brothers.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a son of Jacob.
Joseph was a leader among his brothers.
The LORD blessed Joseph’s land.
The LORD gave Joseph precious dew from heaven above.
The LORD gave Joseph deep waters that lie beneath the earth.
The LORD gave Joseph a bountiful harvest from the sun.
The LORD gave Joseph an abundant yield from the changing seasons.
The LORD gave Joseph the best of the ancient mountains.
The LORD gave Joseph the bounty of the everlasting hills.
The LORD gave Joseph the choice gifts of the land.
The LORD gave Joseph everything in the land.
The LORD showed favor to Joseph.
The LORD is the One who dwelt in the burning bush.
All these blessings rest on the head of Joseph.
These blessings crown the brow of the prince among his brothers.
passages.original: וּלְיוֹסֵ֣ף אָמַ֔ר מְבֹרֶ֥כֶת יְהֹוָ֖ה אַרְצ֑וֹ מִמֶּ֤גֶד שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ מִטָּ֔ל וּמִתְּה֖וֹם רֹבֶ֥צֶת תָּֽחַת׃ וּמִמֶּ֖גֶד תְּבוּאֹ֣ת שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וּמִמֶּ֖גֶד גֶּ֥רֶשׁ יְרָחִֽים׃ וּמֵרֹ֖אשׁ הַרְרֵי־ קֶ֑דֶם וּמִמֶּ֖גֶד גִּבְע֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם׃ וּמִמֶּ֗גֶד אֶ֚רֶץ וּמְלֹאָ֔הּ וּרְצ֥וֹן שֹׁכְנִ֖י סְנֶ֑ה תָּב֙וֹאתָה֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹסֵ֔ף וּלְקָדְקֹ֖ד נְזִ֥יר אֶחָֽיו׃

passages.text: His majesty is like a firstborn bull, and his horns are like those of a wild ox. With them he will gore the nations, even to the ends of the earth. Such are the myriads of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph is like a firstborn bull.
He has great majesty.
His horns are like the horns of a wild ox.
He uses his horns to attack the nations.
He pushes them to the ends of the earth.
Ephraim is very many.
Manasseh is very many.
Ephraim has tens of thousands.
Manasseh has thousands.
passages.original: בְּכ֨וֹר שׁוֹר֜וֹ הָדָ֣ר ל֗וֹ וְקַרְנֵ֤י רְאֵם֙ קַרְנָ֔יו בָּהֶ֗ם עַמִּ֛ים יְנַגַּ֥ח יַחְדָּ֖ו אַפְסֵי־ אָ֑רֶץ וְהֵם֙ רִבְב֣וֹת אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְהֵ֖ם אַלְפֵ֥י מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Zebulun he said: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your journeys, and Issachar, in your tents.
passages.sermon:
Zebulun is a tribe of Israel.
Issachar is also a tribe of Israel.
Moses spoke a blessing about Zebulun and Issachar.
He said, “Zebulun, rejoice when you go out on your journeys.
Issachar, rejoice while you stay in your tents.”
passages.original: וְלִזְבוּלֻ֣ן אָמַ֔ר שְׂמַ֥ח זְבוּלֻ֖ן בְּצֵאתֶ֑ךָ וְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר בְּאֹהָלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: They will call the peoples to a mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness. For they will feast on the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.”
passages.sermon:
Zebulun and Issachar will call the peoples.
They will call them to a mountain.
There, the people will offer sacrifices.
These sacrifices will be righteous.
The people will feast.
They will enjoy the abundance of the seas.
They will also enjoy the hidden treasures of the sand.
passages.original: עַמִּים֙ הַר־ יִקְרָ֔אוּ שָׁ֖ם יִזְבְּח֣וּ זִבְחֵי־ צֶ֑דֶק כִּ֣י שֶׁ֤פַע יַמִּים֙ יִינָ֔קוּ וּשְׂפוּנֵ֖י טְמ֥וּנֵי חֽוֹל׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Gad he said: “Blessed is he who enlarges the domain of Gad! He lies down like a lion and tears off an arm or a head.
passages.sermon:
Gad is a tribe of Israel.
Moses spoke a blessing about Gad.
He said, “Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad’s land.
Gad lives like a lion.
Gad attacks fiercely.
Gad tears off an arm.
Gad tears off a head.”
passages.original: וּלְגָ֣ד אָמַ֔ר בָּר֖וּךְ מַרְחִ֣יב גָּ֑ד כְּלָבִ֣יא שָׁכֵ֔ן וְטָרַ֥ף זְר֖וֹעַ אַף־ קָדְקֹֽד׃

passages.text: He chose the best land for himself, because a ruler’s portion was reserved for him there. He came with the leaders of the people; he administered the LORD’s justice and His ordinances for Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Gad was a tribe of Israel.
Gad chose the best land for himself.
A ruler’s portion was reserved for Gad in that land.
Gad came with the leaders of the people.
Gad carried out the LORD’s justice.
Gad obeyed the LORD’s laws for Israel.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא רֵאשִׁית֙ ל֔וֹ כִּי־ שָׁ֛ם חֶלְקַ֥ת מְחֹקֵ֖ק סָפ֑וּן וַיֵּתֵא֙ רָ֣אשֵׁי עָ֔ם צִדְקַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֖יו עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Concerning Dan he said: “Dan is a lion’s cub, leaping out of Bashan.”
passages.sermon: Moses spoke about the tribe of Dan.\r\nDan is like a young lion.\r\nDan leaps out from Bashan.
passages.original: וּלְדָ֣ן אָמַ֔ר דָּ֖ן גּ֣וּר אַרְיֵ֑ה יְזַנֵּ֖ק מִן־ הַבָּשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: Concerning Naphtali he said: “Naphtali is abounding with favor, full of the blessing of the LORD; he shall take possession of the sea and the south.”
passages.sermon:
Naphtali is a tribe of Israel.
Naphtali has much favor.
Naphtali is full of the LORD’s blessing.
Naphtali will take the sea.
Naphtali will take the south.
passages.original: וּלְנַפְתָּלִ֣י אָמַ֔ר נַפְתָּלִי֙ שְׂבַ֣ע רָצ֔וֹן וּמָלֵ֖א בִּרְכַּ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה יָ֥ם וְדָר֖וֹם יְרָֽשָׁה׃ס

passages.text: And concerning Asher he said: “May Asher be the most blessed of sons; may he be the most favored among his brothers and dip his foot in oil.
passages.sermon:
Asher is a son of Israel.
Moses spoke a blessing about Asher.
Asher will be the most blessed among the sons of Israel.
Asher will be the most favored by his brothers.
Asher will dip his foot in oil.
passages.original: וּלְאָשֵׁ֣ר אָמַ֔ר בָּר֥וּךְ מִבָּנִ֖ים אָשֵׁ֑ר יְהִ֤י רְצוּי֙ אֶחָ֔יו וְטֹבֵ֥ל בַּשֶּׁ֖מֶן רַגְלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: May the bolts of your gate be iron and bronze, and may your strength match your days.”
passages.sermon: Your gates will have bolts of iron and bronze.\r\nYour strength will last as long as your days.
passages.original: בַּרְזֶ֥ל וּנְחֹ֖שֶׁת מִנְעָלֶ֑יךָ וּכְיָמֶ֖יךָ דָּבְאֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: “There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your aid, and the clouds in His majesty.
passages.sermon:
The God of Jeshurun is unique.
No one is like Him.
He helps His people.
He rides through the heavens to give you aid.
He shows His majesty in the clouds.
He is powerful and glorious.
He comes to help you from above.
passages.original: אֵ֥ין כָּאֵ֖ל יְשֻׁר֑וּן רֹכֵ֤ב שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ בְעֶזְרֶ֔ךָ וּבְגַאֲוָת֖וֹ שְׁחָקִֽים׃

passages.text: The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He drives out the enemy before you, giving the command, ‘Destroy him!’
passages.sermon:
God is eternal.
God is your dwelling place.
His arms are everlasting.
God supports you from beneath with His everlasting arms.
God drives out your enemy before you.
God commands, “Destroy him!”
passages.original: מְעֹנָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵי קֶ֔דֶם וּמִתַּ֖חַת זְרֹעֹ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם וַיְגָ֧רֶשׁ מִפָּנֶ֛יךָ אוֹיֵ֖ב וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַשְׁמֵֽד׃

passages.text: So Israel dwells securely; the fountain of Jacob lives untroubled in a land of grain and new wine, where even the heavens drip with dew.
passages.sermon:
Israel is a nation chosen by God.
Israel lives in safety.
Jacob’s descendants live alone and unafraid.
They live in a land filled with grain.
They live in a land filled with new wine.
Even the heavens above give them dew.
God provides for Israel.
God gives Israel peace and abundance.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכֹּן֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל בֶּ֤טַח בָּדָד֙ עֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל־ אֶ֖רֶץ דָּגָ֣ן וְתִיר֑וֹשׁ אַף־ שָׁמָ֖יו יַֽעַרְפוּ טָֽל׃

passages.text: Blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is the shield that protects you, the sword in which you boast. Your enemies will cower before you, and you shall trample their high places.”
passages.sermon:
Israel is a people saved by the LORD.
The LORD is your protector.
He is your shield.
He is your help.
He is the sword in which you boast.
No other nation is like you, Israel.
Your enemies will cower before you.
You will trample on their high places.
You are blessed, Israel.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֶ֨יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל מִ֣י כָמ֗וֹךָ עַ֚ם נוֹשַׁ֣ע בַּֽיהוָ֔ה מָגֵ֣ן עֶזְרֶ֔ךָ וַאֲשֶׁר־ חֶ֖רֶב גַּאֲוָתֶ֑ךָ וְיִכָּֽחֲשׁ֤וּ אֹיְבֶ֙יךָ֙ לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֖ה עַל־ בָּמוֹתֵ֥ימוֹ תִדְרֹֽךְ׃ס
